author: Kels
body:
Honestly, to this day, the community is a bit widespread, and there could be some improvements to make the community together. As mentioned in Turtles "Avicus: Problems, and how to improve thread" located here, he did mention the community once, but did not mention anything about improving the over quality of the current community. Even if the community is smaller in numbers, there are ways we can improve. Here are some:

Tournaments - This can even help with advertising, but that's beside the point. If we host more tournaments, this will bring avicus players' the competitive aspect of minecraft they need. Tournaments are usually hosted within a community to help show competitve aspects within one community. Besides, it's fun.

Teamspeak Discussions - Honestly, this is extremely big. There can be a day where a lot of the regulars on avicus get together in one teamspeak room and discuss about anything. This could be about how to improve Avicus, what's going on in real life or anything else. It should be kept to serious topics in case you're wondering. That way, we can see how people feel behind those faces in minecraft.

Frequent Forum Discussions - Many threads discussing about Avicus would be very nice to improve the community. I saw this happen quite a few times, but was stopped for some odd reason. This should be brought back, as like it said, can bring a community in one spot and completely enhance it.

Daily Map Testing - Gameplay wise, this could really bond a community. People can have fun with this, and give their feedback on a map. This can be hosted in teamspeak, where someone like Para or any other Map Developers would set a map on a server and then have a group of people testing it constantly.

Frequent Annoucements/Updates - As to frequently updating a whole server on what's going on in Avicus, similar to the news, this can tell a community what's going on, and there could possibly be discussions on things. For example, if Avicus added a new map to Nebula02, then people would discuss if it was right. Sort of like the news, except on e-legos.

The community is probably better than 50% of minecraft communities, but it definitely can change. Remember, a community represents your server, and it shows if this server or that server is good enough.

replies.author: ViceTechnicolour
replies.body:
Daily Map Testing 
As a map developer, we were asked to only test maps for events, but the problem is even after extensive testing, the map might just suddenly break and you can't really fix it before the server goes down. It's not really our fault but once it goes down, it usually stays down which it has to be resurrected by Ivy; it's been down for about a month now and it got ME2 cancelled, but I'd love to do more tests.
